quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What can increase fatigue while riding?

options.text: Stopping frequently.
Riding in cool weather.
Being comfortable during your ride.
Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue, dress to protect yourself from tiring weather like wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue can happen when they wear off.

questions.question: About ______ of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking.

options.text: 20 percent
40 percent
60 percent
80 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a major cause of motorcycle crashes and deaths. Studies show that about 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: To reduce your reaction time, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This is especially important when riding through areas with potential hazards.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane to have the most room if a passing vehicle's wind blast affects your motorcycle?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most space to react if a wind blast from a passing vehicle affects your control.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes provide all of the following except:

options.text: Comfort.
Protection in a collision.
Protection from the cold.
Discomfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you in a collision and from weather hazards like heat or cold. They provide comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycle brakes?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal braking power.
The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more braking power than the front brake.
Only the front brake should be used when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake, providing at least 70 percent of your total stopping power. Use both brakes anytime you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the rear of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders behind them watch and help if needed.

questions.question: About hearing protection for motorcycle riders, which is true?

options.text: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Wear hearing protection only on long rides.
Do not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
A helmet provides enough hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs protect your hearing while still allowing you to hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be which of the following?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should you avoid?

options.text: Plan travel segments based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Use a staggered riding formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan routes based on the least experienced rider's skill level. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind the leader so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Just behind the lead rider.
At the back of the group.
Anywhere within the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the lead rider. This way, experienced riders behind them can watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: When riding at night, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Be visible.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam, use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective materials. Move around in your lane to help others see you and keep safe. Do not stay only in the left portion.

questions.question: What collects in the center portion of a traffic lane?

options.text: Debris and oil drippings from cars.
Motorcycle riders should always travel there for safety.
Most accidents happen there.
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil drippings from cars.
questions.explanation: Debris and oil drippings from cars collect in the center of the lane. Hazards like manhole covers are also found there.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride under the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Accelerate before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Near dangerous areas like intersections, cover the clutch lever and both brakes. This puts your hands ready to brake quickly if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?

options.text: Usually more powerful than a car's headlights.
Usually just as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually larger than a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the direction opposite of where you plan to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve left, press the left handle grip, then the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handle grip, then the left.

questions.question: Why should you not ride too far to the right with a sidecar or three-wheeled motorcycle?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side. If you ride too far right, the sidecar can run off the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the right rear wheel may leave the road if you get too close to the edge.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often alcohol is consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much alcohol is consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, health, and food intake may also matter.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?

options.text: Eye contact
Using a turn signal
Following another vehicle
Nothing

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will. Stay alert and defensive.

questions.question: What formation should a group of riders use when entering a curve?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when turning, entering curves, or entering or exiting highways. Staggered formation is best for straight roads where riders can maintain space between them.

questions.question: What color are warning signs, and what color is the lettering?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering
White with black lettering
Red with white lettering
Green with white lettering

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
Reduce the escape routes you have available.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce the escape routes you have available.
questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you see and be seen. It should keep you out of other drivers' blind spots, stop other drivers from sharing your lane, and give you escape routes if danger appears.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride together in groups, can they ride side by side?

options.text: No, they cannot ride side by side.
No, not even when traffic is heavy.
Yes, if both riders agree to it.
Yes, but only on roads with three or more lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if both riders agree to it.
questions.explanation: Nevada law allows two motorcycles to ride side by side in one lane if both riders agree. A staggered formation is usually safer for group riding.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle around a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the middle of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Move your path as needed for the curve.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your path as needed for the curve.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles handle curves differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. You may need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting something in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before you hit it.
Slow down before you hit it.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you hit it.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as you can before hitting the object. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat and ease off the throttle just before impact.
